_about: Published constants for the aurora model of the nightglow stage (nightglow_aurora.py). Each block names its source; values transcribed by hand from the documents named (page images where the text layer is unusable). docs/reports/nightglow.md.

fang2008._source: Fang, X., Randall, C. E., Lummerzheim, D., Solomon, S. C., Mills, M. J., Marsh, D. R., Jackman, C. H., Wang, W. & Lu, G. (2008), Electron impact ionization: A new parameterization for 100 eV to 1 MeV electrons, J. Geophys. Res. 113, A09311, DOI:10.1029/2008JA013384. Eqs. 2, 4, 6, 7 and Table 1 (read from the page image: the text layer drops the minus signs). Open copy: https://acd-ext.gsfc.nasa.gov/People/Jackman/Fang_2008.pdf
fang2008._note: E0 is the characteristic energy of a Maxwellian (mean energy 2 E0); Q0 in keV cm^-2 s^-1; rho in g cm^-3; H = kT/(m g) in cm; 35 eV per ion pair.

n2plus._source: Q_emis of the N2+ first negative (0,0) band at 391.4 nm, 14.8e-18 cm^2 at 100 eV (Doering & Yang best value, Itikawa 2006 Sect. 9.2 and Table 19), and the total ionisation cross section of N2 at 100 eV, 2.51e-16 cm^2 (Itikawa 2006 Table 16): Itikawa, Y. (2006), Cross sections for electron collisions with nitrogen molecules, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 35, 31-53, DOI:10.1063/1.1937426 (NIST copy https://srd.nist.gov/JPCRD/jpcrd697.pdf). The ratio Q_exc(B)/Q_ion is constant within 10 % above 100 eV (same section). Band Einstein coefficients of N2+ B-X (v'=0) by direct integration: Laher's tables (https://web.ipac.caltech.edu/staff/laher/fluordir/N2+_B-X.out, 1999), identical within precision to Gilmore, Laher & Espy (1992), J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 21, 1005, DOI:10.1063/1.555910.
n2plus._note: A01_over_A00 = 3.71e6 / 1.14e7. Band positions are band origins: vacuum wavelength = 1e4 / wavenumber (um).

o1d._source: Transition probabilities: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (Kramida et al.), O I 2s2.2p4 1D2 -> 3P2,1,0 (M1 + E2): 630.0304 nm 5.63e-3 + 2.11e-5 s^-1, 636.3776 nm 1.82e-3 + 3.39e-6 s^-1, 639.1733 nm 8.6e-7 s^-1 (air wavelengths). Quenching: IUPAC preferred values, Atkinson, R. et al. (2004), Evaluated kinetic and photochemical data for atmospheric chemistry: Volume I - gas phase reactions of Ox, HOx, NOx and SOx species, Atmos. Chem. Phys. 4, 1461-1738, DOI:10.5194/acp-4-1461-2004 (summary table rows 36 and I.A1.3): O(1D) + N2 1.8e-11 exp(107/T) (100-350 K), O(1D) + O2 3.2e-11 exp(67/T) (200-350 K), cm^3 molecule^-1 s^-1. Used at thermospheric temperatures beyond the evaluated range (extrapolation). Quenching by O and by electrons is not included.

oi5577._source: NIST Atomic Spectra Database: O I 2s2.2p4 1D2 - 1S0, 557.7339 nm (air).

gabrielse2021._source: Gabrielse, C., Nishimura, T., Chen, M., Hecht, J. H., Kaeppler, S. R., Gillies, D. M., Reimer, A. S., Lyons, L. R., Deng, Y., Donovan, E. & Evans, J. S. (2021), Estimating precipitating energy flux, average energy, and Hall auroral conductance from THEMIS all-sky-imagers with focus on mesoscales, Frontiers in Physics 9, 744298, DOI:10.3389/fphy.2021.744298 (CC BY). Fig. 2B: B3C electron-transport results (Strickland et al.) for Maxwellian precipitation in an MSIS90 atmosphere (Fort Smith, 16 Feb 2010), green/blue (557.7/427.8) against red/blue (630.0/427.8) for 30 average energies (listed beside the figure) and oxygen scaling factors fO. Read here for fO = 1.00 (the reference O/N2): each E line traced from its foot on the fO = 0.25 curve to the fO = 1.00 curve (image analysis of the figure's embedded 1350 x 1151 px image; axes calibrated on the decade ticks: x = 409.5 + 212.5 log10(R/B), y = 801 - 345.2 log10(G/B / 10)). E = 3.67 and 4.69 keV and E above 9.81 keV could not be separated and are left out.
gabrielse2021.readingUncertainty: about +-3 px in x and y, i.e. +-3 % in R/B and +-2 % in G/B; the energy assignment assumes the 29 E-line feet detected on the fO = 0.25 curve plus its left end are the table's 30 energies in order

whiter2023._source: Whiter, D. K., Partamies, N., Gustavsson, B. & Kauristie, K. (2023), The altitude of green OI 557.7 nm and blue N2+ 427.8 nm aurora, Ann. Geophys. 41, 1-12, DOI:10.5194/angeo-41-1-2023 (CC BY). 57 907 simultaneous triangulated peak emission heights, MIRACLE all-sky cameras (northern Finland and Sweden, 2000-2007, solar zenith angle > 101 deg, IL < -50 nT).
whiter2023._use: Check only (tests and report): the model's peak heights at typical OVATION average energies are compared with these measured means; nothing is fitted to them.

op2010._source: Newell, P. T., Sotirelis, T. & Wing, S. (2009), Diffuse, monoenergetic, and broadband aurora: The global precipitation budget, J. Geophys. Res. 114, A09207, DOI:10.1029/2009JA014326; Newell, P. T., Sotirelis, T. & Wing, S. (2010), Seasonal variations in diffuse, monoenergetic, and broadband aurora, J. Geophys. Res. 115, A03216, DOI:10.1029/2009JA014805. Coupling function: Newell, P. T., Sotirelis, T., Liou, K., Meng, C.-I. & Rich, F. J. (2007), A nearly universal solar wind-magnetosphere coupling function inferred from 10 magnetospheric state variables, J. Geophys. Res. 112, A01206, DOI:10.1029/2006JA012015. IDL release by NOAA NCEI (Redmon, Machol, Case; sourceforge.net/projects/ovation-prime), its coefficient files and algorithm as ported to Python in OvationPyme (Kilcommons).
